heading: INT. SLEEPER CAR - ORIENT NIGHT EXPRESS - 2 A.M.

units.text: INT. SLEEPER CAR - ORIENT NIGHT EXPRESS - 2 A.M.
Gaslight steady.
Curtains drawn.
The train hammers through a tunnel.
PRUDENCE ACHTERBERG, 50s, in a quilted robe, grips a teacup.
Across from her, COLONEL ISAAC DUBOIS-KANE, 70, in pajamas and monocle, thumbs a revolver.
LALITA SENGUPTA, 20s, a porter's daughter in borrowed uniform, stands guard by the door.
ENZO MARCHETTI, 30s, a violinist, sits sweating by the window.
CECILE VANTERPOOL, 40s, in evening gown, lies on the floor between them.
Not moving.
Colonel, put that down. You'll shoot the wrong one.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: There is no wrong one, madam. Only the guilty and the uncooperative.
units.name: DUBOIS-KANE

units.text: It was her wine, I tell you. She drank first.
units.name: ENZO

units.text: She did not drink first. You poured.
units.name: LALITA

units.text: I poured for everyone!
units.name: ENZO

units.text: You poured for her twice.
units.name: LALITA

units.text: Lalita, dear, you are the only one not drinking.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: I'm on shift, Madam Achterberg.
units.name: LALITA

units.text: Then why do you stand at the door?
units.name: DUBOIS-KANE

units.text: Because the last one to leave a murder is the first one accused.
units.name: LALITA

units.text: A long beat.
The train bucks.
The cup rattles in its saucer.
Cecile's fingers twitch.
Colonel. Her hand.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: By Jove. She's alive.
units.name: DUBOIS-KANE

units.text: Of course I'm alive. Someone get me out of this dress.
units.name: CECILE
